'''''Dinebra panicea''''' is a plant [[species]] belonging to the family [[Poaceae]].

==Description==

[[Inflorescences]] are much-branched [[panicles]] in which the [[Spikelet| spikelets']] uppermost florets (tiny grass flowers with no petals) are reduced to small rudiments, and the spikelets themselves separate above the [[glumes]] at maturity. Leaf sheaths (leaf bases clasping the stems) bear long hairs with bulbous bases, and [[ligules]] at leaf bases are conspicuous, membranous, topped with a fringe of hairs, and irregularly toothed, as seen below:

==Distribution==

On the [[iNaturalist]] distribution map for ''Dinebra panicea'', observations of the species are documented -- both in its native areas and as an [[Invasive species| invasive]] -- in the Americas from the central US south to Chile and Brazil, southern Asia, and spottily elsewhere in Africa, Europe, Australia and Oceania.<ref>{{cite web
| title = Mucronate Sprangletop(''Dinebra panicea'')
| url = https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/898439-Dinebra-panicea
| website = inaturalist.org
| access-date = August 29, 2025}}</ref>

==Habitat==

Both subspecies ''panicea'' and ''brachiata'' are described as occurring in wetlands, swamps, or streams in open lowland regions, as well as waste places, gardens and rice fields.<ref name="pier" /><ref name="aus" /> In the southeastern US, subspecies ''mucronata'' is said to occur on sandy shores and in disturbed areas.<ref>{{cite book
| last = Weakley
| first = A.S.
| title = Flora of the Southeastern United States Web App.
| publisher = University of North Carolina Herbarium, North Carolina Botanical Garden
| edition = 2025
| date = 2025
| location = Chapel Hill, North Carolina, US
| url = https://fsus.ncbg.unc.edu/main.php?pg=show-taxon-detail.php&taxonid=2114
| access-date = August 27, 2025}}</ref>

==Ecology==

In the [[Great Plains]] region of the US, ''Dinebra panicea'' is designated as a facultative wetland species, meaning that usually it occur in [[wetlands]], but may occur in non-wetlands.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://wetland-plants.sec.usace.army.mil/static/reports/NWPL%20Cover%20Page%20GP_v3.pdf
| title = National Wetland Plant List Great Plains Region
| date = 2022
| website = army.mil
| publisher = US Army Corps of Engineers National Wetland Plant List National Panel1
| access-date = August 27, 2025}}</ref> It is listed as a weed by the  International Livestock Research Institute.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://genebank.ilri.org/gringlobal/taxon/taxonomydetail?id=465468
| title = Taxon: ''Dinebra panicea'' (Retz.) P. M. Peterson & N. Snow subsp. ''panicea''
| date = 10 June 2021
| website = ilri.org
| publisher = International Livestock Research Institute
| access-date = August 27, 2025}}</ref>

==Etymology==

The genus name ''Dinebra'' is a corruption of the Arabic word ''danaiba'', meaning "a little tail," possibly alluding to the tapering, or acuminate, tips of the spikelets' glumes.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://keys.lucidcentral.org/keys/v3/AusGrass/key/AusGrass/Media/Html/gendesc/Dinebra.htm
| title = Dinebra
| date = July 2002
| website = lucidcentral.org
| publisher = AusGrass: Grasses of Australia
| access-date = August 27, 2025}}</ref>

In 1783, [[Anders Jahan Retzius]] probably chose to use the species name ''panicea'' because the grass's spikelets are arranged in a large, classic [[panicle]]. The word "panicle" derives from the Latin ''panicula'', which is the diminutive form of ''panus'', meaning "ear of millet." [[Millet]] is a general name applying to several small-seeded grasses producing edible grains; most millets belong to the grass tribe [[Paniceae]], whose species produce panicle-type inflorescences.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://worldofsucculents.com/botanical-terms/panicle/
| title = Browsing: panicle
| website = worldofsucculents.com
| publisher = World of Succulents
| access-date = August 27, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
| title = ''Poaceae Tribe Paniceae''
| url = https://floranorthamerica.org/Poaceae_tribe_Paniceae
| website = floranorthamerica.org
| access-date = August 27, 2025}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==

In many texts, ''Dinebra panicea'' is treated as ''Leptochloa filiformis''.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://auth1.dpr.ncparks.gov/flora/species_account.php?id=3876
| title = Vascular Plants of North Carolina; Account for Red Sprangletop - ''Dinebra panicea'' (Retzius) P.M. Peterson & N. Snow= 
| website = ncparks.gov
| publisher = The North Carolina Biodiversity Project
| access-date = August 25, 2025}}</ref>

In 2021, after a detailed genetic study of several genera of the subtribe Eleusininae, the genus ''Dinebra'', which for most of the century incorporated 3 species, was enlarged to ±23 species. ''Dinebra'' and the 27 other genera in the Eleusininae appear to have originated in Africa.<ref>{{cite journal
| last = Peterson
| first = Paul M.
| last2 = Romaschenko
| first2 = Konstantin
| last3 = Herrra Arrieta
| first3 = Yolanda
| last4 = Vorontsova
| first4 = Maria S.

| journal = Journal of Systematics and Evolution
| volume = 60

}}</ref>

===Subspecies===
''Dinebra panicea'' contains the following subspecies:<ref name="kew"></ref>
* ''Dinebra panicea'' subsp. ''mucronata'' <small>(Steud.) P.M.Peterson & N.Snow (2012)</small> -- the Americas
* ''Dinebra panicea'' subsp. ''panicea'' -- tropical and subtropical Asia
* ''Dinebra panicea'' subsp. ''brachiata'' <small>(Steud.) P.M.Peterson & N.Snow (2012)</small> -- the Americas
